institutions: Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit, University College London
Interdisciplinary Center for Neural Computation, Hebrew University

conditions: choice problem in which two learned controllers can assign different values or uncertainty to the same candidate action
task: select an action using predictions of long-run future outcomes under changing task structure and training history
temporal_scope: controller estimates change with experience; one controller can recompute after outcome changes while the other relies on stored summaries

nodes.description: controller that stores scalar long-run action-value summaries learned from experience
controller that estimates long-run value by chaining learned short-term transition and outcome predictions at choice time
action whose long-run value is estimated by both controllers
scalar expected future value supplied by the stored-summary controller
expected future value computed by searching predicted successor states and outcomes
estimated uncertainty associated with the stored-summary controller's action-value prediction
estimated uncertainty associated with the forward-search controller's prediction, including uncertainty introduced by approximate search
which controller's action recommendation governs behavior in the current circumstance

relations.description: the stored-summary controller maps a state-action situation to a cached scalar long-run value without representing the full sequence of future consequences
the forward-search controller maps the same state-action situation to a long-run value by composing predicted transitions and outcomes
which controller dominates depends on their relative estimated uncertainty, favoring the controller expected to be more accurate
the two controllers can use the same task state, action and reward inventory while differing in computational topology, flexibility, cost and uncertainty profile
